habitat: Cuban crocodiles are found exclusively in Cuba, primarily in the Zapata Swamp and Lanier Swamp on the Isle of Youth. They inhabit freshwater marshes, swamps, and flooded forests. With a range of less than 500 square kilometers, they have the smallest geographic distribution of any living crocodilian. Their preferred habitat is densely vegetated freshwater wetlands with deep pools and floating vegetation mats. They are among the most terrestrial crocodilians, frequently hunting and traveling on land.
diet: Cuban crocodiles are agile, opportunistic predators specializing in terrestrial prey unusual for crocodilians — including hutias (tree-dwelling rodents), birds, turtles, fish, and occasionally wild pigs and deer. They employ a unique hunting behavior: launching themselves out of the water with powerful tail-propelled leaps to snatch low-flying birds and arboreal mammals from overhanging branches. Juveniles feed on insects, amphibians, and small fish.
behavior: Cuban crocodiles are considered the most aggressive New World crocodilian and among the most intelligent crocodilians — they have been observed engaging in cooperative pack-hunting, a behavior extremely rare among reptiles. In captivity, they are known for their bold personalities and responsiveness to keepers. They are highly terrestrial, basking and traveling significant distances on land. Males are territorial and engage in violent combat. Females lay 20-40 eggs in mound nests. They are more active and visibly curious than most crocodilians.
facts: Cuban crocodiles are the most critically endangered crocodilian in the Americas — fewer than 3,000-5,000 remain in the wild. They are exceptionally agile, capable of galloping on land at surprising speeds. Their scales often display a distinctive 'pearly' pattern — a yellow-orange speckling that gives them one of the most beautiful crocodilian skins. They readily hybridize with American crocodiles, threatening their genetic integrity. Cuba maintains a successful captive breeding program.
naming: Cuban crocodile names might reflect their Cuban origin or agile hunting style. Consider names like Cuba, Fidel, Havana, Pearl, Speckle, Leaper, Swampy, Zapata, Carib, or Crock.
